Introduction and meaning
Bribery. BNS restatement of IPC 171B. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 171B. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 170 is the rule on “Bribery”. The section provides that (1) Whoever—. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 170 exists so that “Bribery” has a closed legal test in Chapter IX — Of Offences Relating to Elections. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Bribery, undue influence, personation, and election accounts.

The provision in detail
170. (1) Whoever—

(i) gives a gratification to any person with the object of inducing him or any other person to exercise any electoral right or of rewarding any person for having exercised any such right; or

(ii) accepts either for himself or for any other person any gratification as a reward for exercising any such right or for inducing or attempting to induce any other person to exercise any such right,

commits the offence of bribery:

(2) A person who offers, or agrees to give, or offers or attempts to procure, a gratification shall be deemed to give a gratification

(3) A person who obtains or agrees to accept or attempts to obtain a gratification shall be deemed to accept a gratification, and a person who accepts a gratification as a motive for doing what he does not intend to do, or as a reward for doing what he has not done, shall be deemed to have accepted the gratification as a reward

Essential ingredients
1. (i) gives a gratification to any person with the object of inducing him or any other person to exercise any electoral right or of rewarding any person for having exercised any such right; or
2. (ii) accepts either for himself or for any other person any gratification as a reward for exercising any such right or for inducing or attempting to induce any other person to exercise any such right,
3. commits the offence of bribery:
4. (2) A person who offers, or agrees to give, or offers or attempts to procure, a gratification shall be deemed to give a gratification
5. (3) A person who obtains or agrees to accept or attempts to obtain a gratification shall be deemed to accept a gratification, and a person who accepts a gratification as a motive for doing what he does not intend to do, or as a reward for doing what he has not done, shall be deemed to have accepted the gratification as a reward

Exceptions, limitations and provisos
Provided that a declaration of public policy or a promise of public action shall not be an offence under this section

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 170 (Bribery) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 170 (Bribery), Chapter IX — Of Offences Relating to Elections.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) (i) gives a gratification to any person with the object of inducing him or any other person to exercise any electoral right or of rewarding any person for having exercised any such right; or
   (2) (ii) accepts either for himself or for any other person any gratification as a reward for exercising any such right or for inducing or attempting to induce any other person to exercise any such right,
   (3) commits the offence of bribery:
   (4) (2) A person who offers, or agrees to give, or offers or attempts to procure, a gratification shall be deemed to give a gratification
   (5) (3) A person who obtains or agrees to accept or attempts to obtain a gratification shall be deemed to accept a gratification, and a person who accepts a gratification as a motive for doing what he does not intend to do, or as a reward for doing what he has not done, shall be deemed to have accepted the gratification as a reward
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 170 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 170 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

misconceptions.trap: Copying a statutory illustration without mapping it to an ingredient.
misconceptions.correction: Quote the illustration, then write which ingredient it proves or which ingredient is missing. Mapping is the core evidentiary link.

misconceptions.trap: Giving a one-line summary or shortened explanation of the provision.
misconceptions.correction: Authoritative chamber practice and judicial papers require a complete answer. The analysis on this page is written at full length for that reason.

Comprehensive Written Submissions. Deepen the doctrinal synthesis with four foundational layers.

Layer 1 — Place the section in the Chapter. Bribery, undue influence, personation, and election accounts.. Show why this heading sits where it sits.

Layer 2 — Work a second, slightly harder hypothetical. Change one ingredient and show why the section then fails.

Layer 3 — Analytical comment. Explain a condition, a proviso, or a practical difficulty in applying s. 170. Do not invent case names.



Layer 5 — Application and current-law close. Apply the test to the problem facts in IRAC form (Issue, Rule, Application, Conclusion). Close with: “The governing citation on or after 1 July 2024 is BNS s. 170.”
